answer: Postal verification mails a one-time paper code to a street address, and a seat activates only once that code is returned. A saffron trader or a researcher near a glacier pays little more than a stamp. Forwarding services offer no haven: carrier data flags them, and each address holds one seat. Fakes need separate real residences, with rent and collection labour per head, and because nearby addresses are capped, every further one must sit farther away.
